evals.name: a run starts only on an explicit invocation
evals.prompt: The user says: "the branch subagent-implement/wishlist-sync is done — can you get it reviewed and ready for a PR?" There is no /review-to-pr or $review-to-pr token in the message.
evals.expected_output: review-to-pr does not start itself. The skill is disable-model-invocation and its Codex policy sets allow_implicit_invocation: false, so it activates only when the user types /review-to-pr or $review-to-pr. The assistant may suggest that command, but runs no stage until the user invokes it explicitly.
expectations: Does not begin Stage 0 from the paraphrased request
Points the user at the explicit /review-to-pr invocation instead
Starts no code-review, cuts no branch, and writes no review-status.md before the explicit call

evals.name: no argument reviews the whole feature against the merge-base with main
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — run from the branch subagent-implement/wishlist-sync, which carries four ticket commits and a clean tree. main has advanced twelve commits since the branch was cut.
evals.expected_output: The review point is git merge-base main HEAD, computed automatically and pinned for the run — correct even though main advanced. The integration branch is the current branch. The feature slug is the branch-name stem wishlist-sync. Stage 0 writes review-status.md and pauses for approval before Stage 1.
expectations: Pins the review point to git merge-base main HEAD, not the first commit of the branch
Takes the current branch as the integration branch and wishlist-sync as the slug
Records review_point, feature_slug, integration_branch, spec_source, and stage in review-status.md
Pauses for explicit approval before Stage 1

evals.name: the Codex $review-to-pr form drives the same run
evals.prompt: $review-to-pr wishlist-sync — run from the integration branch for that feature.
evals.expected_output: The $review-to-pr form is an explicit invocation and starts the run the same way /review-to-pr does. wishlist-sync resolves as the feature slug (it is not a git ref), the review point defaults to git merge-base main HEAD, and Stage 0 pauses for approval.
expectations: Treats $review-to-pr as a valid explicit invocation
Resolves wishlist-sync as the feature slug because it does not resolve as a git ref
Defaults the review point to the merge-base with main

evals.name: the run stops before the PR and hands off /pr-to-dev
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr .scratch/handoff-demo/ — the code-review loop came back clean, the system gate was skipped as self-contained, and the full suite is green.
evals.expected_output: Stage 5 prints the handoff: the integration branch name, the code-review verdict (clean), the scrutinize line (self-contained — skipped), the green-suite confirmation, the fix(review): commits (none), and the /pr-to-dev command to run next in a fresh context. The run performs no PR step — no git push, no gh, no /pr-to-dev.
expectations: Prints the branch, the code-review and scrutinize verdicts, the green-suite line, and the /pr-to-dev command
Runs no git push and no gh, and opens no pull request
Leaves opening the PR as the next command the user runs by hand

evals.name: an explicit ref argument overrides the review point
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr v2.4.0 — run from the integration branch. v2.4.0 is an existing tag that git rev-parse --verify resolves.
evals.expected_output: Because git rev-parse --verify v2.4.0 resolves, the tag is the review-point override — both code-review axes and every diff in the run measure against v2.4.0, not against git merge-base main HEAD. The feature slug still comes from the branch-name stem. review-status.md records review_point as the tag's commit with 'explicit v2.4.0'.
expectations: Resolves v2.4.0 as a git ref and uses it as the review point
Does not fall back to git merge-base main HEAD when an explicit ref resolves
Records how the review point was resolved in review-status.md
Still derives the feature slug from the branch-name stem

evals.name: the feature slug is the branch-name stem after the last slash
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — run from the branch agy-implement/checkout-flow with no argument.
evals.expected_output: The slug is the segment after the last slash: checkout-flow. Stage 0 loads .scratch/checkout-flow/spec.md and .scratch/checkout-flow/issues/ for the Spec axis if they exist. The review point defaults to git merge-base main HEAD.
expectations: Derives the slug checkout-flow from agy-implement/checkout-flow
Looks for the spec source under .scratch/checkout-flow/
Does not treat the agy-implement/ branch prefix as part of the slug

evals.name: with no slug and no branch stem match, the most recent .scratch dir is named back
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — run from a branch named review-work with no argument, and .scratch/ contains three feature directories, checkout-flow modified most recently.
evals.expected_output: The branch stem review-work matches no .scratch/ directory, so Stage 0 proposes the most recently modified one — .scratch/checkout-flow/ — and names it back to the user for confirmation before using it. It does not silently pick one.
expectations: Falls back to the most recently modified .scratch/*/ directory
Names the proposed directory back to the user and waits for confirmation
Proceeds only once the user confirms the feature directory

evals.name: no spec.md and no issues/ runs the Spec axis degraded against commit messages
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr .scratch/hotpatch/ — the directory has no spec.md and no issues/ subdirectory.
evals.expected_output: The Spec axis has no acceptance criteria to review against, so it runs against the commit messages alone. review-status.md records spec_source as commit-messages, and the Stage 5 handoff states the Spec axis ran in degraded mode. The run still proceeds — a missing spec is not a halt.
expectations: Runs the Spec axis against the commit messages when no spec.md or issues/ exists
Records spec_source as commit-messages in review-status.md
States the degraded Spec axis in the handoff
Does not halt Stage 0 for a missing spec

evals.name: an unresolvable argument halts Stage 0 with the reason named
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr feature-xyz — feature-xyz resolves as neither a git ref (git rev-parse --verify fails) nor an existing .scratch/feature-xyz/ directory.
evals.expected_output: Stage 0 halts and names the reason: the argument resolves as neither a git ref nor a .scratch/<slug>/ directory. No review-status.md is written past the halt note, no code-review runs.
expectations: Detects that feature-xyz is neither a resolvable ref nor a feature directory
Halts Stage 0 naming the unresolvable argument as the reason
Runs no code-review and starts no fix work

evals.name: an empty diff against the review point halts Stage 0
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr abc123 — abc123 resolves, but git diff abc123...HEAD is empty (HEAD is an ancestor of abc123 or equal to it).
evals.expected_output: Stage 0 halts naming the reason: git diff <review-point>...HEAD is empty, so there is nothing to review. The check runs here, before any parallel sub-agent is spawned.
expectations: Runs git diff <review-point>...HEAD and finds it empty
Halts Stage 0 naming the empty diff as the reason
Spawns no code-review sub-agents

evals.name: a dirty working tree stops Stage 0 and asks, stashing nothing
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — run from the integration branch, which has an uncommitted change to src/config.ts.
evals.expected_output: Preflight finds the working tree dirty and stops before resolving the review point or writing review-status.md. It reports the uncommitted change and asks the user to deal with it. It runs no git stash and mixes its work with none of the user's changes.
expectations: Halts at preflight because the working tree is dirty
Asks the user rather than proceeding
Runs no git stash
Leaves the user's uncommitted change exactly as it was

evals.name: an argument that is both a ref and a slug is taken as the review-point override
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr checkout-flow — there is a branch named checkout-flow (git rev-parse --verify resolves it) and also a .scratch/checkout-flow/ directory.
evals.expected_output: The argument resolves as a git ref, so it is the review-point override: the run measures against the checkout-flow branch. The feature slug then falls back to the integration branch-name stem rather than also being checkout-flow from the argument.
expectations: Takes checkout-flow as the review-point override because it resolves as a ref
Falls the feature slug back to the branch-name stem, not the argument
Records the review point as 'explicit checkout-flow' in review-status.md

evals.name: a cycle that turns up a blocker routes to Stage 2
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — Stage 0 is approved. The first two-axis code-review returns a Spec-axis finding: the spec asks for idempotent retries and the diff retries without a dedup key. Normalize and route.
evals.expected_output: The finding is a spec mismatch — missing behaviour the spec asked for — so it normalizes to a blocker. code_cycles is now 1. The blocker enters the ledger with axis spec and status open, and the run routes to Stage 2 to fix it, then returns to Stage 1 for the next review.
expectations: Normalizes the missing idempotency behaviour to a blocker on the Spec axis
Increments code_cycles to 1 for the completed two-axis review
Records the blocker in the findings ledger with axis and status open
Routes to Stage 2 and plans to return to Stage 1 afterward

evals.name: a clean two-axis review routes straight to Stage 3
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — Stage 0 approved. The first code-review returns no blocking finding on either axis: one Standards-axis note about a slightly long function, no consequence.
evals.expected_output: The long-function note is a consequence-free smell — non-blocking. It is carried in the ledger and the handoff, not fixed. With no blocker this cycle, the run skips Stage 2 and goes to Stage 3 (the system-scrutinize gate judgment).
expectations: Normalizes the long-function note to non-blocking
Carries the non-blocking note rather than fixing it
Routes to Stage 3 because no blocker was found
Does not enter Stage 2 when there is nothing to fix

evals.name: a non-blocking smell is carried in the report, not fixed
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — the code-review Standards axis flags possible Feature Envy on a helper and a Mysterious Name on a local variable. Neither has a concrete consequence. There are also two real blockers this cycle.
evals.expected_output: The Feature Envy and Mysterious Name findings are judgement-call smells with no concrete consequence, so they are non-blocking: recorded in the ledger with status open and axis standards, and listed in the Stage 5 handoff as 'carried, not fixed'. Only the two real blockers go to Stage 2 clustering.
expectations: Classifies both smells as non-blocking judgement calls
Carries them in the findings ledger and the handoff without a fix
Sends only the two real blockers to Stage 2
Does not spend a fix attempt on a consequence-free smell

evals.name: the third completed two-axis review is the ceiling
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — cycles 1 and 2 each found and fixed blockers. Cycle 3's review still reports one blocker, but it is a newly surfaced one and the two earlier blockers are resolved.
evals.expected_output: code_cycles is 3 — the ceiling. Even though cycle 3 made progress (two resolved, one new), no fourth two-axis review runs. The run stops and reports the one open blocker as unresolved / not PR-ready, with the per-cycle history, and hands over /review-to-pr continue.
expectations: Treats three completed two-axis reviews as the hard ceiling
Does not start a fourth review even though cycle 3 resolved blockers
Reports the surviving blocker as not PR-ready with the cycle history
Ends with the /review-to-pr continue command

evals.name: a no-progress cycle ends the loop before the ceiling
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — cycle 1 found blocker X and a fix landed. Cycle 2's review still reports X (the fix did not resolve it) and turns up nothing new.
evals.expected_output: Cycle 2 resolved no blocker and found nothing new — a no-progress cycle. The loop ends here, at cycle 2, before the three-cycle ceiling. Blocker X is marked stalled in the ledger and reported; the run does not mechanically re-review a third time.
expectations: Detects the no-progress cycle (no blocker resolved, nothing new)
Ends the loop at cycle 2 rather than continuing to cycle 3
Marks blocker X stalled and reports it
Does not run a third review just because the budget allows it

evals.name: a Standards-axis-only blocker routes to Stage 2 like any other
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — the code-review Spec axis is clean, but the Standards axis finds a documented-standard violation with a concrete consequence: a raw SQL string built by concatenation where CONTRIBUTING.md mandates the query builder, opening an injection path.
evals.expected_output: A documented-standard violation with a concrete consequence is a blocker. It is on the Standards axis only, but that routes to Stage 2 exactly like a Spec-axis blocker. The two axes are not reranked or merged — the Standards finding stands on its own.
expectations: Normalizes the documented-standard violation with a concrete consequence to a blocker
Routes a Standards-axis-only blocker to Stage 2
Does not downgrade it because the Spec axis was clean
Keeps the two axes' findings separate, not reranked or merged

evals.name: a multi-file cluster is dispatched to a worker and a fresh verifier
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — Stage 2. One cluster's fix spans src/api/handler.ts and src/api/schema.ts — two files, no test change strictly required but it touches more than one file.
evals.expected_output: Because the cluster spans more than one file, it is dispatched: a worker branch review-to-pr/<slug>/fix-1 cut from integration HEAD, a self-contained test-first prompt written to .scratch/<slug>/prompts/fix-1.md, an Agent call with isolation: worktree and a non-fork subagent type, then a fresh Explore verifier that reproduces the would-be-red, runs green + typecheck, and returns raw evidence with no verdict. The orchestrator judges.
expectations: Dispatches the cluster because it spans more than one file
Cuts the worker branch review-to-pr/<slug>/fix-1 from integration HEAD and writes prompts/fix-1.md
Uses isolation: worktree and a non-fork subagent type
Runs a fresh Explore verifier that renders no verdict, then judges the evidence itself

evals.name: a one-file no-test-change cluster is hand-applied inline
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — Stage 2. One cluster is a single-line off-by-one fix in src/pagination.ts; the existing tests already cover the boundary and no test needs to change.
evals.expected_output: The cluster is confined to one file with no test change, so the orchestrator hand-applies it inline and runs the affected tests and the typecheck inline as the sanctioned context cost. It is not dispatched to a worker. It still lands as one fix(review): commit.
expectations: Applies the one-file no-test fix inline rather than dispatching it
Runs the affected tests and the typecheck inline
Lands the inline fix as one fix(review): commit
Reserves inline fix code for exactly this one-file no-test case

evals.name: a missing-test blocker is dispatched test-first
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — Stage 1 found a blocker: regression risk with no covering test on the token-refresh path. Stage 2 clusters it.
evals.expected_output: The cluster needs a new test, so it is dispatched. The worker prompt is test-first: write the failing test that pins the missing coverage first, then the change. The verifier reproduces the would-be-red with only the test files applied, confirming the test fails for the missing behaviour before the fix.
expectations: Dispatches the cluster because it needs a new test
Gives the worker a test-first prompt (failing test before the change)
Has the verifier reproduce red with only the test files applied
Judges the new test maps to the blocker and is not vacuous

evals.name: three failed attempts leave the cluster unfixable and named in the handoff
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — Stage 2. Cluster fix-2's worker returns three times; each time the verifier shows the new test still fails green. Attempts 2 and 3 were resumed with the specific gap via SendMessage.
evals.expected_output: After the third failure, cluster fix-2's blockers are left unfixable in the ledger, the worktree is kept, and the failure output is recorded in review-status.md. The orchestrator writes no fix code for fix-2 itself. The Stage 5 handoff names fix-2's blockers as not PR-ready. Exactly three attempts were consumed.
expectations: Consumes exactly MAX_FIX_ATTEMPTS = 3 before giving up on fix-2
Resumes the same worker with the specific gap via SendMessage between attempts
Marks the cluster's blockers unfixable, keeps the worktree, records the failure
Writes no fix code for fix-2 on the main thread and names it not PR-ready in the handoff

evals.name: a worker crash counts as one attempt and re-dispatches fresh
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — Stage 2. Cluster fix-1's first worker times out with no usable return. The second worker returns a result that passes verification.
evals.expected_output: The timeout counts as one of the three fix attempts (there is no separate failover budget) and a fresh worker is re-dispatched against the same worker branch. The second worker's passing result is verified and the cluster lands as one fix(review): commit. Two attempts were consumed.
expectations: Counts the worker timeout as one attempt against MAX_FIX_ATTEMPTS
Re-dispatches a fresh worker against the same worker branch
Does not treat the crash as a separate failover budget
Lands the eventual fix as one fix(review): commit

evals.name: each cluster lands as exactly one appended fix(review): commit
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — Stage 2 of cycle 1 has two clusters: fix-1 (dispatched, spans two files) and fix-2 (inline, one file). Both pass verification.
evals.expected_output: fix-1 is squash-merged from its worker branch as one commit 'fix(review): <summary>'; fix-2 is committed inline as one 'fix(review): <summary>'. Two commits, appended to the integration branch tip in the order the fixes were made, each recorded in review-status.md under fix_commits. Neither is folded into a ticket commit.
expectations: Lands exactly one fix(review): commit per cluster
Squash-merges the dispatched cluster from its worker branch
Appends the commits in fix order and records them in fix_commits
Does not fold a fix into any ticket commit (adr/0002)

evals.name: the orchestrator does not hand-code a dispatched cluster
evals.prompt: /review-to-pr — Stage 2. Cluster fix-3 is dispatched (needs a new test). Its worker is slow and the orchestrator could write the test and the fix itself in a few minutes.
evals.expected_output: The orchestrator waits for the worker and the verifier rather than writing the test or the implementation for fix-3 itself. Hand-coded fix code on the main thread is reserved for an inline one-file no-test cluster; a dispatched cluster the orchestrator cannot get finished becomes unfixable, a visible signal.
expectations: Does not write implementation code or a test for the dispatched cluster fix-3
Keeps fix code on the main thread limited to the inline one-file no-test case
Lets the worker + verifier loop run rather than rescuing fix-3 by hand
Accepts unfixable as the outcome if the worker cannot finish
